title: Transient Access Pass prototype + enterprise contract / SQ preflight pathway
creator: Hannah Lee
description: Build and validate a short-lived "Transient Access Pass" (TAP) that grants expanded free-tier credits and feature flags for 14 days, combined with a lightweight enterprise contract & Security Questionnaire (SQ) preflight path that surfaces likely legal/compliance blockers early in the PLG funnel. Goal: reduce friction for mid-market/enterprise trials while preserving contract gating and legal intake efficiency.
hypotheses: H1: A 14-day TAP with augmented credits (+30%) and temporary feature flags will increase activation to 1st meaningful token by 20% among self-serve signups from target segments.
H2: Early, inline SQ preflight (3-question flow) will reduce long-form legal intake and shorten time-to-SOW for enterprise by 25% without significantly increasing churn among dev teams.

H3: Sales-assisted conversion rate from TAP->paid will be neutral or improved compared to baseline if we route TAP accounts with high SQ risk to AE outreach rather than immediate contract negotiation.
metrics: Activation: % of TAP users hitting 1st meaningful token within 72h
Engagement: Avg daily tokens consumed during TAP window
Sales lead quality: % TAP flagged as enterprise-SQ risk -> accepted by AE
Support overhead: Incidents / legal inquiries per 100 TAPs
acceptance_criteria: TAP infra: token-based pass provisioning endpoint and admin dashboard to issue/revoke TAPs
Billing: credits applied to user account and visible in cost breakdown during TAP period
SQ UI: embedded 3-question preflight in signup flow; results stored to customer profile
Routing: TAP accounts with SQ risk create a lead in Salesforce/HubSpot and set 'enterprise_preflight' flag
Observability: dashboard showing activation/engagement/conversion metrics by cohort
design_decisions: Pass duration set to 14 days (tradeoff: long enough to try features, short enough to limit cost exposure)
Augmented credits set to +30% relative to current free-tier allocation (conservative uplift to guard unit economics)
SQ preflight limited to 3 binary questions to avoid creating friction while surfacing red flags
Default TAP routing: low-risk -> standard PLG funnel; high-risk -> AE outreach + legal intake
implementation_notes: Backend: new /taps POST endpoint in accounts-service (ENG-4021), idempotent token creation
Console: temporary 'Active TAP' banner on account overview; link to TAP expiration countdown
Billing: reuse existing credit bucket logic (billing-service pr: github.com/redwood/billing/pull/198) with TAP tag
SQ data stored in customer-profile (encrypted at rest); KMS access requested (SEC-req-77)

Design: CTA & SQ microcopy + mobile/responsive mockups (Figma: Redwoods/TAP-frames)
Engineering: backend endpoint, account flag, credit allocation, dashboard telemetry

comments: 2026-02-16 | Hannah Lee: Initial discovery — pulled in growth, sales, and legal. Evidence from last quarter: several mid-market signups stalled in contract phase after initial trial run. Proposal: give a short, higher-value trial plus an early SQ to triage.

2026-02-22 | Miguel Ortega: Technical review w/ infra. ENG concerns: need to ensure TAP credit accounting doesn't double-count with promo codes. Action: ENG-4021 to add dedupe and single-source-of-truth for credit buckets.

2026-02-28 | Priya Raman (Legal): Reviewed SQ draft. Suggested adding minimal non-binding checkbox about data residency to capture red flags. Also requested retention TTL of 12 months for preflight answers. Assigned follow-up to legal@redwood.

2026-03-03 | Jordan Patel (Sales): Suggested routing rule: if company size > 500 or self-identified PII use case -> auto-create AE lead and set priority. Also requested CSV export for CRM ingestion. Created sales-playbook draft at drive link.
2026-03-08 | Design feedback (Sara Kim): Microcopy A preferred in user tests (n=10) — language reduces perceived friction vs. full-length SQ. We'll A/B test microcopy A vs B across first 3k TAPs.

2026-03-10 | Miguel Ortega: Spike complete for TAP endpoint; PR opened (github.com/redwood/accounts/pull/412). Backend tests + e2e smoke pass in staging. Need frontend QA and security review before can schedule canary rollout.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: TAP could be abused to drain free credits — Mitigation: rate limits per account and one TAP per billing entity
Risk: SQ adds friction and reduces PLG conversion — Mitigation: keep SQ minimal and optional; A/B test with control cohort
Risk: Legal backlog if many flagged TAPs — Mitigation: route to AE for triage and limit auto-escalations to high-severity signals only

Complete security review and KMS provisioning (owner: SecOps)
Schedule 2-week canary in EU region for 1k TAPs
Instrument cohort dashboards and set alert for unexpected cost delta > 15% vs baseline
